Q: Batch script to find directory of folder? A: 
@ECHO OFF
SETLOCAL
rem The following setting for the directory is a name
rem that I use for testing and deliberately includes spaces to make sure
rem that the process works using such names. These will need to be changed to suit your situation.

SET "sourcedir=u:\your files"
SET "existingdir=dira"
SET "newdir=dirb"
SET "parent="

FOR /d /r "%sourcedir%" %%e IN (*) DO IF "%%~nxe"=="%existingdir%" SET "parent=%%~dpe"&MD "%%~dpe%newdir%" 2>NUL >nul
:firstonly
:: remove trailing '\' from pathname
IF DEFINED parent SET "parent=%parent:~0,-1%"
ECHO parent is "%parent%"

GOTO :EOF

This code should do what you arrear to want. It should create "newdir" under every "existingdir" found in the subtree "sourcedir".

'parent' is set to the last-directory-created's parent. I remove the final backslash because building names with manually-inserted directory-separators is usually easier.

Note that directory-separators in Windows are backslashes, not forward-slashes.

Append &GOTO firstonly to the for/d… line to create the new directory in the first-found original only.

2>nul >nul suppresses [error] reports from the md operation.

Q: What is in Angular the correct term of a public property in an object component that contains form data or display data? A:

The model is only the "json object".

We talk about "form-model" to reference to the "control". It's more easy understand when you use ReactiveForms or FormSignal: the "form-model" is the formGroup or the form signal (a complex object with properties of value, binding, valuesChange...

When use [ngModel] you create also a NgControl with these properties about value, binding valueChange..., (but it's some "transparent" because you use a directive in the .html). You can say that "item.name" it's not only a property of item, else a NgControl, or a "form-model" of this property.

So, item is only a model and it's not related to the server (can be,e.g. a variable)

Q: Exploring an AI control architecture that governs LLM and agent behavior — looking for expert feedback A:

I’ve thought about similar patterns in production systems, so here’s my take.

The direction makes sense, even if the idea itself isn’t new. What you’re really doing is drawing a hard line between “LLM suggests” and “system acts.” Most agent frameworks blur that boundary, and making the decision layer explicitly deterministic is where your approach actually adds value.

This doesn’t solve alignment in a philosophical sense, but it avoids a large class of failures by assuming the model can be wrong and refusing to give it authority. That shifts the problem to rule design and validation, which is still hard, but much more tractable.

One clear benefit is hallucination handling. If the LLM proposes something incorrect, a governance layer that validates actions against real constraints can simply block it. The model’s confidence becomes irrelevant because the final decision isn’t its responsibility.

Where this fits best is in systems that require auditability and clear accountability—regulated domains, internal automation, or any workflow involving irreversible actions. In those cases, being able to point to a specific rule matters more than flexibility.

The main risk is brittleness. The system can only enforce what you’ve anticipated, and as rules grow, maintenance becomes harder. Simulation-first execution also assumes you can accurately simulate outcomes, which isn’t always realistic.

Overall, this looks strongest as a narrowly scoped control layer rather than a general-purpose solution for all agents.

Q: ValueError: KivyMD: App object must be inherited from `kivymd.app.MDApp` A:

So apparently my issue wasn't with the textfield, it was theme manager. so instead of

import kivymd
from kivy.app import App
from kivymd.app import MDApp
from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
from kivymd.theming import ThemeManager
from kivymd.uix.textfield import MDTextField


class MainApp(MDApp):

    theme_cls = ThemeManager()
    theme_cls.primary_palette = "Blue"
    theme_cls.theme_style = "Dark"

MainApp().run()

I was supposed to use

import kivymd
from kivy.app import App
from kivymd.app import MDApp
from kivy.uix.floatlayout import FloatLayout
from kivymd.uix.textfield import MDTextField


class MainApp(MDApp):
    def __init__(self, **kwargs):
        self.title = "BMI"
        self.theme_cls.theme_style = "Dark"
        self.theme_cls.primary_palette = "Blue"
        super().__init__(**kwargs)

MainApp().run()

Q: In single-thread Rust, what's the most idiomatic or concise way to mut borrow one field in a struct and leave the rest available? A:

The fundamental problem is that you have a self-referential struct. You may want to search for that term online; there's plenty of content. But basically, this is one thing that Rust just doesn't do well. It's inherently counter to the ownership model. I think your second example is probably going to be the best option. If you find yourself making maybe such slicing structs, you may consider writing a macro to create them for you. (The macro could take the struct name and the fields it needs to extract, and then generate the struct and a From impl.)
